rows.why: The part of S1 that is a real open question is what happens when a new code collides with an existing one. Item 7 asks that. Its pick redraws, and the run shows repeated redraws before giving up, which matches 'drawn again'. The 14-day lifetime is taken as given rather than asked by any item.
Item 12 asks what a redeemed code shows about who used it and when. The run shows usedBy 'alice' and a usedAt timestamp after redeeming, which matches 'shows it was used by c1, and when'.
Item 5 asks whether case, spacing or hyphens matter when matching a typed code. The run redeemed a lowercased, padded, re-hyphenated version and got ok:true, so it was treated as the same code.
Item 1 asks whether a code is still valid at exactly 14 days. The run shows 'unused' at 14 days minus 1 ms, then 'expired' and reason 'expired' at exactly 14 days, which is what S4 expects.

S5 turns on whether the same contributor can redeem their own used code again as a harmless repeat. No item asks that. Item 2 is about a different, unused code for a task the contributor already has, which is S7. Item 3 is about which reason wins when several apply.
Item 4 asks about revoking unknown, used and already-revoked codes. The run shows revoking a used code throws 'invite code has been used', which matches 'a used code cannot be revoked'.
Item 2 asks what happens when a contributor who already has access redeems another code. The run returned reason 'already has access' and the second code stayed 'unused'.
Item 11 asks how simultaneous operations on one code are handled. The run used a store with random delays: exactly one redeem succeeded and the others failed with 'used'.

What sets S9 apart is that a used code stays 'used' after its expiry time. Item 3 asks which state wins when a code is both used and expired. The run redeemed a used code at day 15 and got reason 'used', not 'expired'. This tests redeem rather than list, but it is the same question of which state wins.
